title: Valmiki Ramayana — Ayodhya Kanda
source_owner: Ralph T. H. Griffith translation (1870-1874) via Project Gutenberg; Sanskrit companion-only
revision_note: P1 Starter canonical ingestion per RAMAYANA_CANONICAL_SOURCE_PLAN.md Stage 1: Griffith public domain translation, Sanskrit companion-only.

content.sanskrit:
गच्छता मातुलकुलं भरतेन तदानघः ।
शत्रुघ्नो नीतवान् वीरो भ्रातृस्नेहेन चावृतः ॥
content.transliteration:
gacchatā mātulakulaṃ bharatena tadānaghaḥ |
śatrughno nītavān vīro bhrātṛsnehena cāvṛtaḥ ||
content.text: When to his maternal grandfather's home Bharata went, the sinless hero took with him Shatrughna out of deep brotherly affection.
content.translation: When to his maternal grandfather's home Bharata went, the sinless hero took with him Shatrughna out of deep brotherly affection.
content.provenance: Griffith (1870-1874), Book II, Canto I. Project Gutenberg #51540 (public domain). Sanskrit companion-only.

content.sanskrit:
स हि रूपोपपन्नश्च वीर्यवाननसूयकः ।
भूमौ समभवत् श्रेष्ठो रामः सत्यपराक्रमः ॥
content.transliteration:
sa hi rūpopapannaśca vīryavānanasūyakaḥ |
bhūmau samabhavat śreṣṭho rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ ||
content.text: Endowed with beauty, valor, and freedom from malice, Rama was the foremost on earth, of unfailing truth and righteous prowess.
content.translation: Endowed with beauty, valor, and freedom from malice, Rama was the foremost on earth, of unfailing truth and righteous prowess.
content.provenance: Griffith (1870-1874), Book II, Canto I. Project Gutenberg #51540 (public domain). Sanskrit companion-only.

content.sanskrit:
स च नित्यं प्रशान्तात्मा मृदुपूर्वं च भाषते ।
उच्यमानोऽपि परुषं नोत्तरं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
content.transliteration:
sa ca nityaṃ praśāntātmā mṛdupūrvaṃ ca bhāṣate |
ucyamāno'pi paruṣaṃ nottaraṃ pratipadyate ||
content.text: Serene in mind, he ever spoke gentle words first; even when addressed with harsh speech, he would never utter a harsh retort.
content.translation: Serene in mind, he ever spoke gentle words first; even when addressed with harsh speech, he would never utter a harsh retort.
content.provenance: Griffith (1870-1874), Book II, Canto I. Project Gutenberg #51540 (public domain). Sanskrit companion-only.

content.text: Skilled in arms and archery, he constantly spent his leisure in conversation with elders venerable in character, wisdom, and age.
content.translation: Skilled in arms and archery, he constantly spent his leisure in conversation with elders venerable in character, wisdom, and age.
content.provenance: Griffith (1870-1874), Book II, Canto I. Project Gutenberg #51540 (public domain). Sanskrit companion-only.

content.sanskrit:
अनुमन्यध्वमस्मत्तः सर्वानेवाहमामन्त्रये ।
कथं वा क्रियतां किं वा सर्वैरेवं विमृश्यताम् ॥
content.transliteration:
anumanyadhvamasmattaḥ sarvānevāhamāmantraye |
kathaṃ vā kriyatāṃ kiṃ vā sarvairevaṃ vimṛśyatām ||
content.text: I address you all, my counselors and lords: if it pleases you, grant your approval that Rama be anointed heir, or deliberate what else is best for the realm.
content.translation: I address you all, my counselors and lords: if it pleases you, grant your approval that Rama be anointed heir, or deliberate what else is best for the realm.
content.provenance: Griffith (1870-1874), Book II, Canto II. Project Gutenberg #51540 (public domain). Sanskrit companion-only.

content.sanskrit:
अहं हि वचनाद्राज्ञः पतेयमपि पावके ।
भक्षयेयं विषं तीक्ष्णं मज्जेयमपि चार्णवे ॥
content.transliteration:
ahaṃ hi vacanādrājñaḥ pateyamapi pāvake |
bhakṣayeyaṃ viṣaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ majjeyamapi cārṇave ||
content.text: At the bidding of my sire and king, I would cast myself into blazing fire, swallow deadly poison, or plunge into the depths of the ocean.
content.translation: At the bidding of my sire and king, I would cast myself into blazing fire, swallow deadly poison, or plunge into the depths of the ocean.
content.provenance: Griffith (1870-1874), Book II, Canto XVIII. Project Gutenberg #51540 (public domain). Sanskrit companion-only.

content.sanskrit:
तद् ब्रूहि वचनं देवि राज्ञा यदभिकाङ्क्षितम् ।
करिष्ये प्रतिजाने च रामो द्विर्नाभिभाषते ॥
content.transliteration:
tad brūhi vacanaṃ devi rājñā yadabhikāṅkṣitam |
kariṣye pratijāne ca rāmo dvirnābhibhāṣate ||
content.text: Therefore speak the word, O Queen, which the King desires; I promise I will fulfill it without fail. Rama ne'er speaks twice.
content.translation: Therefore speak the word, O Queen, which the King desires; I promise I will fulfill it without fail. Rama ne'er speaks twice.
content.provenance: Griffith (1870-1874), Book II, Canto XVIII. Project Gutenberg #51540 (public domain). Sanskrit companion-only.

content.sanskrit:
एवमस्तु गमिष्यामि वनं वस्तुमहं त्वितः ।
जटाचीरधरो राज्ञः प्रतिज्ञामनुपालयन् ॥
content.transliteration:
evamastu gamiṣyāmi vanaṃ vastumahaṃ tvitaḥ |
jaṭācīradharo rājñaḥ pratijñāmanupālayan ||
content.text: So let it be: I will depart hence to dwell in the forest, wearing bark and matted hair, upholding my father's solemn vow.
content.translation: So let it be: I will depart hence to dwell in the forest, wearing bark and matted hair, upholding my father's solemn vow.
content.provenance: Griffith (1870-1874), Book II, Canto XIX. Project Gutenberg #51540 (public domain). Sanskrit companion-only.

content.sanskrit:
सत्यमेवेश्वरो लोके सत्ये धर्मः सदा श्रितः ।
सत्यमूलानि सर्वाणि सत्यान्नास्ति परं पदम् ॥
content.transliteration:
satyameveśvaro loke satye dharmaḥ sadā śritaḥ |
satyamūlāni sarvāṇi satyānnāsti paraṃ padam ||
content.text: Truth alone is the sovereign Lord in the world; on truth righteousness ever rests. All things are rooted in truth; there is no status or state higher than truth.
content.translation: Truth alone is the sovereign Lord in the world; on truth righteousness ever rests. All things are rooted in truth; there is no status or state higher than truth.
content.provenance: Griffith (1870-1874), Book II, Canto CIX. Project Gutenberg #51540 (public domain). Sanskrit companion-only.
